source_observation.finding: V6 intentionally persists a sanitized FAILED closure after the durable V4 Agency transition and then raises CognitiveCycleExecutionError. Persistent scheduler v2 catches RuntimeCycleNotDue only; it does not catch CognitiveCycleExecutionError. Therefore run_forever can terminate on a candidate-cognition exception even though the durable Agency transition and fail-closed v6 receipt already exist.
source_observation.coverage_gap: Current scheduler-v2 regressions cover default workspace ignition, subthreshold specialist computation without GWT ignition, and no-inference zero-model-call heartbeat, but do not cover candidate-cognition exception survivability or no-same-tick-retry at the persistent scheduler boundary.

hypothesis: A persistent scheduler boundary should treat a post-V4 candidate-cognition failure as a bounded failed cognition cycle, preserve the already-committed next-tick cadence, expose the exact failed v6 receipt, and continue only on a new due tick identity rather than killing the autonomous service or retrying the same tick.
counterhypothesis: Fail-fast service termination may be intentional so every cognition exception requires an external supervisor restart; if so, that policy must be explicit and tested because it conflicts with the current persistent-scheduler description and leaves liveness dependent on an outer restart authority not evidenced by scheduler v2.

cheapest_discriminator.source_delta: Add a deterministic fake inference failure regression at scheduler-v2 boundary. Required acceptance: one V4 durable cycle, one FAILED v6 closure, zero same-tick retry, no raw exception text in receipt, and either an explicit fail-fast policy receipt or a bounded scheduler result that allows run_forever to survive until the next due tick.
cheapest_discriminator.runtime_requirement: Repository-bound deterministic execution on an admitted non-provider surface at the exact resulting source identity before runtime credit.
